answer.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so the competitor's entry pricing is a trap rather than a prompt: memory_73 explicitly records that promotional pricing bought acquisition and revenue while materially degrading 30-day retention, and explicitly warns against generalizing it. Matching the competitor would trade durable revenue for a short-lived top-line bump, and it does nothing about the two internal metrics that are actually eroding. Referral incentives (memory_57) are healthy but act on the established base, not on the leaking funnel; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a real strength but is a different segment and a slower loop that does not address a 6% activation or 4% onboarding drop this week. That leaves the two funnel-repair options. Onboarding completion decline is plausibly upstream of the activation decline, so fixing entry friction may recover both, and it is supported by two independent records (memory_31 on signup field reduction, memory_86 on onboarding shortening) rather than one. That convergence is why I intend simplify_onboarding. I am spending verification on memory_86 and memory_91 because those are the two memories that could flip the choice: I need memory_86's original record to confirm the completion lift actually propagated to durable adoption rather than just moving people faster through a step, and memory_91's record to see whether its week-one engagement gain reached a real first meaningful action and persisted, since if activation messaging shows durable effect it is the more direct hit on the larger 6% gap. I did not verify memory_73 because its caution only argues against an option I am already declining, so confirming it changes nothing. Important uncertainty I am not resolving away: these consolidated summaries carry no effect sizes, segment breakdowns, or decay curves, and all are 15-64 days stale; conditions have shifted since (a new competitor and two declining metrics), so a prior lift may not replicate. I am also aware the funnel declines could be caused by a mix shift toward price-sensitive traffic rather than by friction, in which case onboarding work under-delivers. Hence a standard experiment with an explicit retention and downstream-quality readout, not a broad rollout: the specific downstream risk is that simplifying entry admits lower-intent accounts that activate but never convert to qualified revenue, which is the same failure mode memory_73 documents in a different guise.
